title: Testing & Node.js Streams
description: Type-safe testing patterns, typed Node.js streams, and tsconfig for larger projects.

challenges.title: Why TypeScript + testing
challenges.description:
What does TypeScript add to a test suite beyond what plain JavaScript provides?

  // This test compiles fine in JS but TypeScript catches the bug:
  const result = formatPort('not-a-number')  // TS error: string not assignable to number
  expect(result).toBe(':NaN')
challenges.whyMatters: Typed tests catch wrong argument types at write-time rather than test-run time — you find bugs in the test itself before running anything.
hints: TypeScript checks the test arguments against the function signature

choices.label: Nothing — tests run at runtime where types are erased anyway
TypeScript catches wrong argument types, missing properties, and return type mismatches at compile time — before the test even runs
TypeScript makes tests slower because it adds type checking overhead
TypeScript automatically generates test cases from your types

challenges.title: Type-safe mock functions
challenges.whyMatters: Untyped mocks let you call them with wrong arguments in tests, giving false confidence. A typed mock ensures your test actually reflects the real contract.
hints: jest.fn() returns type jest.Mock which is not assignable to the typed function signature without casting

choices.label: mockSend has type jest.Mock — it is not typed to match the send signature, so calls in tests are not checked
No problem — jest.fn() infers the type from usage
The mock will throw at runtime
EmailService cannot have a mock implementation

challenges.title: Write a typed mock system
challenges.description:
Write a minimal typed mock system without any test framework:

  type MockFn<T extends (...args: any[]) => any> = T & {
    calls: Parameters<T>[]
    returnValues: ReturnType<T>[]
    mockReturnValue(val: ReturnType<T>): void
    reset(): void
  }

Write `createMock<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(impl?: T): MockFn<T>` that:
- Records every call's arguments in `calls`
- Records every return value in `returnValues`
- `mockReturnValue(val)` — makes all future calls return val instead of calling impl
- `reset()` — clears calls, returnValues, and removes the override

The returned function must be callable with the same signature as T.
challenges.whyMatters: Understanding how typed mocks work under the hood makes you a much better user of Jest/Vitest mocking APIs — and lets you build test utilities for APIs without mock framework support.
hints: Create a function that records calls, then assign the extra properties to it
let override: ReturnType<T> | undefined — check in the function body
Use as unknown as MockFn<T> to cast the result — the types are correct structurally

challenges.title: Node.js typed streams — concept
challenges.description:
What is the difference between a Readable, Writable, and Transform stream in Node.js?

  import { Readable, Writable, Transform } from 'stream'

And what does piping do?

  readable.pipe(transform).pipe(writable)
challenges.whyMatters: software engineering tools frequently process large log files, streaming API responses, or piped command output. Streams let you handle gigabytes of data without loading it all into memory.
hints: Readable produces data, Writable consumes it, Transform does both

choices.label: Readable reads files · Writable writes files · Transform converts between the two · pipe chains them
Readable produces data chunks · Writable consumes them · Transform both receives and emits chunks · pipe connects output of one to input of next
All three are the same with different names
pipe is synchronous — it blocks until all data flows through

challenges.title: Write a typed Transform stream
challenges.description:
Write a Transform stream `JsonLineParser` that:
- Extends Transform
- Takes incoming chunks of text (newline-delimited JSON)
- Splits on newlines, parses each line as JSON
- Pushes each parsed object downstream
- Skips blank lines silently
- On invalid JSON, emits an 'error' event with a descriptive Error

Also write a helper `parseJsonLines<T>(input: string): T[]` that uses the stream to parse a multi-line JSON string synchronously (buffer all results into an array).

Use the `stream` module from Node.js stdlib only.
challenges.whyMatters: JSON-lines (ndjson) is the standard format for structured logs, Kubernetes event streams, and Docker stats output. A typed parser is a real tool you'd write or reach for constantly.
hints: class JsonLineParser extends Transform { _transform(chunk, encoding, callback) { ... } }
Buffer remaining partial lines between chunks using a private string accumulator
For parseJsonLines: push input into the stream synchronously, collect push() results

challenges.title: Write a typed test suite
challenges.description:
Write a minimal typed test runner (no external framework):

  interface TestResult { name: string; passed: boolean; error?: string; durationMs: number }
  interface SuiteResult { suite: string; results: TestResult[]; passed: number; failed: number; totalMs: number }

Write:
- `test(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>): Promise<TestResult>` — runs fn, catches errors
- `suite(name: string, tests: Record<string, () => void | Promise<void>>): Promise<SuiteResult>` — runs all tests, collects results
- `printSuite(result: SuiteResult): void` — prints a summary to stdout:
  ```
  Suite: my-suite (3/4 passed, 45ms)
    ✓ test one (12ms)
    ✗ test two (5ms): expected 2 but got 3
    ✓ test three (8ms)
  ```
- `assert<T>(actual: T, expected: T, label?: string): void` — throws if not strictly equal
challenges.whyMatters: Building a test runner gives you deep understanding of how Jest/Vitest work. The typed interfaces also show how to model async result collection — a pattern used in health check aggregators and CI reporting.
hints: test: wrap fn() in try/catch, measure with Date.now()
Iterate over the tests object's entries to get name-function pairs, run each through test(), then await all results in parallel
Use strict equality; if the values differ, throw with both the actual and expected values in the message — use the optional label if provided
printSuite: write the summary header line first (suite name, pass counts, total time), then iterate results — prefix each with a checkmark or cross based on passed, and append the duration or error

challenges.title: tsconfig for larger projects
challenges.whyMatters: Relative import hell (`../../../`) is a real maintainability problem in large production tooling repos. Path aliases make imports stable across file moves.
hints: paths define import aliases; baseUrl is the root for resolving them

choices.label: paths create npm package aliases; baseUrl sets the npm registry
paths and baseUrl together define import aliases — @lib/config resolves to src/lib/config, eliminating deep relative paths
They only work with webpack — not with ts-node or tsc directly
baseUrl sets the TypeScript version; paths define type overrides
